target_clause: These registries [SHALL be/are] collected under a "Hypertext Transfer Protocol version 3 (HTTP/3) Parameters" heading.

target_clause: Similarly, the first Initial packet sent after receiving a Retry packet MUST be sent in a single IP packet.
previous_clause: Clients MUST ensure they send the first Initial packet in a single IP packet.
next_clause: The payload of a UDP datagram carrying the first Initial packet MUST be expanded to at least 1200 bytes, by adding PADDING frames to the Initial packet and/or by coalescing the Initial packet (see [packet-coalesce]).

target_clause: If the token is invalid then the server SHOULD proceed as if the client did not have a validated address, including potentially sending a Retry.

next_clause: Tokens provided with NEW_TOKEN frames and Retry packets can be distinguished by servers (see [token-differentiation]), and the latter validated more strictly.

target_clause: A receiver MUST treat the receipt of any other type of frame as a stream error of type HTTP_INTERRUPTED_HEADERS.

next_clause: (Note that QUIC can intersperse data from other streams between frames, or even during transmission of frames, so multiplexing is not blocked by this requirement.)

target_clause: A receiver MUST NOT wait for a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame before sending MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA, since doing so will mean that a sender will be blocked for at least an entire round trip, and potentially for longer if the peer chooses to not send STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frames.
previous_clause: To avoid blocking a sender, and to reasonably account for the possibility of loss, a receiver should send a MAX_DATA or MAX_STREAM_DATA frame at least two round trips before it expects the sender to get blocked.

target_clause: The initial client packet SHOULD be padded to exactly these values unless the client has a reasonable assurance that the PMTU is larger.
previous_clause: In the absence of extensions to the IP header, padding to exactly these values will result in an IP packet that is 1280 octets.
next_clause: Sending a packet of this size ensures that the network path supports an MTU of this size and helps reduce the amplitude of amplification attacks caused by server responses toward an unverified client address.

target_clause: The anti-replay mitigations in [HTTP-REPLAY] MUST be applied when using HTTP/3 with 0-RTT.
previous_clause: The use of 0-RTT with HTTP/3 creates an exposure to replay attack.
next_clause: When applying [HTTP-REPLAY] to HTTP/3, references to the TLS layer refer to the handshake performed within QUIC, while all references to application data refer to the contents of streams.

next_clause: An endpoint MUST treat a TLS renegotiation as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.

target_clause: An endpoint MUST ensure that packets with Destination Connection ID field values that correspond to a reused Stateless Reset Token are attributed to the same connection as long as the Stateless Reset Token is still usable, even when the connection ID has been retired.

next_clause: Otherwise, an attacker might be able to send a packet with a retired connection ID and cause the endpoint to produce a Stateless Reset that it can use to disrupt the connection, just as with the attacks in [reset-oracle].

target_clause: Clients MUST NOT discard responses as a result of receiving such a RST_STREAM, though clients can always discard responses at their discretion for other reasons.
previous_clause: When this is true, a server MAY request that the client abort transmission of a request without error by sending a RST_STREAM with an error code of NO_ERROR after sending a complete response and closing its stream.

target_clause: If the maximum datagram size changes during the connection, the initial congestion window SHOULD be recalculated with the new size.

next_clause: If the maximum datagram size is decreased in order to complete the handshake, the congestion window SHOULD be set to the new initial congestion window.

target_clause: The values provided by a peer for these transport parameters MUST match the values that an endpoint used in the Destination and Source Connection ID fields of Initial packets that it sent.
previous_clause: If it sends a Retry packet, a server also includes the Source Connection ID field from the Retry packet in the retry_source_connection_id transport parameter.
next_clause: Including connection ID values in transport parameters and verifying them ensures that that an attacker cannot influence the choice of connection ID for a successful connection by injecting packets carrying attacker-chosen connection IDs during the handshake.

target_clause: Unused flags MUST be ignored on receipt and MUST be left unset (0x0) when sending.
previous_clause: Unused flags are those that have no defined semantics for a particular frame type.
next_clause: Reserved:: A reserved 1-bit field.

target_clause: It MAY either be a database lookup key or a self-encrypted and self-authenticated value.
previous_clause: The ticket itself is an opaque label.
next_clause: Section 4 of [RFC5077] describes a recommended ticket construction mechanism.

next_clause: In comparison, a token obtained in a Retry packet MUST be used immediately during the connection attempt and cannot be used in subsequent connection attempts.

target_clause: A client MUST use the same cryptographic handshake message it includes in this packet.

next_clause: A server MAY treat a packet that contains a different cryptographic handshake message as a connection error or discard it.

target_clause: The client MAY drop these packets, or MAY buffer them in anticipation of later packets that allow it to compute the key.

next_clause: If a client receives a packet that uses a different version than it initially selected, it MUST discard that packet.

target_clause: All registrations made by Standards Track publications MUST be permanent.
previous_clause: For instance, a provisional registration for a frame type of 61 could be requested.
next_clause: All registrations in this document are assigned a permanent status and list a change controller of the IETF and a contact of the QUIC working group (quic@ietf.org).

target_clause: The HANDSHAKE_DONE frame MUST be retransmitted until it is acknowledged.
previous_clause: PING and PADDING frames contain no information, so lost PING or PADDING frames do not require repair.
next_clause: Endpoints SHOULD prioritize retransmission of data over sending new data, unless priorities specified by the application indicate otherwise; see [stream-prioritization].

target_clause: The client MAY send any requests for which the client considers the server authoritative.
previous_clause: Once a connection exists to a server endpoint, this connection MAY be reused for requests with multiple different URI authority components.
next_clause: An authoritative HTTP/3 endpoint is typically discovered because the client has received an Alt-Svc record from the request's origin which nominates the endpoint as a valid HTTP Alternative Service for that origin.

target_clause: Logged or otherwise persistently stored debug data MUST have adequate safeguards to prevent unauthorized access.
previous_clause: Debug information could contain security- or privacy-sensitive data.

target_clause: An endpoint that receives a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with a sequence number smaller than the Retire Prior To field of a previously received NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame MUST immediately send a corresponding RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame that retires the newly received connection ID.
previous_clause: Once a sender indicates a Retire Prior To value, smaller values sent in subsequent NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames have no effect. A receiver MUST ignore any Retire Prior To fields that do not increase the largest received Retire Prior To value.

target_clause: However, implementations MAY choose to offer the ability to deliver data out of order to a receiving application.
previous_clause: QUIC makes no specific allowances for delivery of stream data out of order.
next_clause: An endpoint could receive data for a stream at the same stream offset multiple times.

target_clause: Unlike TCP, QUIC can detect the loss of these packets and MAY use that information to adjust the congestion controller or the rate of ACK-only packets being sent, but this document does not describe a mechanism for doing so.
previous_clause: Similar to TCP, packets containing only ACK frames do not count towards bytes in flight and are not congestion controlled.
next_clause: The algorithm in this document specifies and uses the controller's congestion window in bytes.

target_clause: Values above the maximum flow-control window size of 231-1 MUST be treated as a connection error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
previous_clause: This setting affects the window size of all streams (see [InitialWindowSize]).
next_clause: SETTINGS_MAX_FRAME_SIZE (0x5):: Indicates the size of the largest frame payload that the sender is willing to receive, in units of octets.

target_clause: Endpoints MUST treat the receipt of a TLS KeyUpdate message as a connection error of type 0x10a, equivalent to a fatal TLS alert of unexpected_message; see [tls-errors].
previous_clause: Endpoints MUST NOT send a TLS KeyUpdate message.
next_clause: [ex-key-update] shows a key update process, where the initial set of keys used (identified with @M) are replaced by updated keys (identified with @N).

target_clause: An endpoint MAY terminate the connection if an alternative path cannot be found.

next_clause: Each pair of local and remote addresses could have a different PMTU.

target_clause: An endpoint that receives a HEADERS frame that causes its advertised concurrent stream limit to be exceeded MUST treat this as a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR or REFUSED_STREAM.
previous_clause: Endpoints MUST NOT exceed the limit set by their peer.
next_clause: The choice of error code determines whether the endpoint wishes to enable automatic retry (see [Reliability] for details).

target_clause: A PUSH_PROMISE frame without the END_HEADERS flag set MUST be followed by a CONTINUATION frame for the same stream.
previous_clause: END_HEADERS (0x4):: When set, the END_HEADERS flag indicates that this frame contains an entire field block and is not followed by any CONTINUATION frames.
next_clause: A receiver MUST treat the receipt of any other type of frame or a frame on a different stream as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.

target_clause: A connection MAY be accepted without address validation - or with only limited validation - but a server SHOULD limit the data it sends toward an unvalidated address.
previous_clause: In response to receiving the token, a server can either abort the connection or permit it to proceed.
next_clause: Successful completion of the cryptographic handshake implicitly provides proof that the client has received packets from the server.

target_clause: The server MAY include either an explicit expiration time or an issued timestamp and dynamically calculate the expiration time.
previous_clause: Thus, a token SHOULD include an expiration time.
next_clause: It is also unlikely that the client port number is the same on two different connections; validating the port is therefore unlikely to be successful.

target_clause: Prior to confirming the handshake, a peer might be unable to process 1-RTT packets, so an endpoint SHOULD send CONNECTION_CLOSE in both Handshake and 1-RTT packets.
previous_clause: Sending a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame in an Initial packet makes it more likely that the server can receive the close signal, even if the application error code might not be received.
next_clause: A server SHOULD also send CONNECTION_CLOSE in an Initial packet.

target_clause: Promised requests MUST conform to the requirements in Section 8.2 of [HTTP2].
previous_clause: The header of the request message is carried by a PUSH_PROMISE frame (see [frame-push-promise]) on the request stream which generated the push.
next_clause: Each pushed response is associated with one or more client requests.

target_clause: A PRIORITY frame that contains more or fewer fields, or a PRIORITY frame that includes a truncated integer encoding MUST be treated as a connection error of type HTTP_MALFORMED_PRIORITY.
previous_clause: A PRIORITY frame MUST contain only the identified fields.

target_clause: If the client has already sent requests on streams with a Stream ID greater than or equal to that indicated in the GOAWAY frame, those requests will not be processed and MAY be retried by the client on a different connection.
previous_clause: Some requests might already be in transit.
next_clause: The client MAY cancel these requests.

target_clause: If the ClientHello spans multiple Initial packets, such servers would need to buffer the first received fragments, which could consume excessive resources if the client’s address has not yet been validated. To avoid this, servers MAY use the Retry feature (see Section 8.1 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT]) to only buffer partial ClientHello messages from clients with a validated address.
previous_clause: Servers might need to parse the entire ClientHello (e.g., to access extensions such as Server Name Identification (SNI) or Application Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN)) in order to decide whether to accept the new incoming QUIC connection.
next_clause: QUIC packet and framing add at least 36 bytes of overhead to the ClientHello message.

target_clause: Duplicate suppression MUST happen after removing packet protection for the reasons described in Section 9.3 of [QUIC-TLS].
previous_clause: A receiver MUST discard a newly unprotected packet unless it is certain that it has not processed another packet with the same packet number from the same packet number space.
next_clause: Endpoints that track all individual packets for the purposes of detecting duplicates are at risk of accumulating excessive state.

target_clause: A TLS implementation MUST NOT automatically re-send early data unless the negotiated connection selects the same ALPN protocol.
previous_clause: A TLS implementation SHOULD NOT automatically re-send early data; applications are in a better position to decide when re-transmission is appropriate.

target_clause: An endpoint SHOULD discard its handshake keys as soon as it has confirmed the handshake.
previous_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT discard its handshake keys until the TLS handshake is confirmed ([handshake-confirmed]).
next_clause: Most application protocols will send data after the handshake, resulting in acknowledgements that allow both endpoints to discard their handshake keys promptly.

target_clause: The alert level of all TLS alerts is “fatal”; a TLS stack MUST NOT generate alerts at the “warning” level.
previous_clause: The resulting value is sent in a QUIC CONNECTION_CLOSE frame.

target_clause: Clients MUST NOT offer TLS versions older than 1.3.
previous_clause: This is acceptable provided that the features of TLS 1.3 that are used by QUIC are supported by the newer version.
next_clause: A badly configured TLS implementation could negotiate TLS 1.2 or another older version of TLS.

target_clause: An endpoint SHOULD NOT send a stateless reset that is significantly larger than the packet it receives.
previous_clause: More unpredictable bytes might be necessary if the endpoint could have negotiated a packet protection scheme with a larger minimum AEAD expansion.
next_clause: Endpoints MUST discard packets that are too small to be valid QUIC packets.

target_clause: To avoid a deadlock, a sender SHOULD ensure that other frames are sent periodically in addition to PADDING frames to elicit acknowledgments from the receiver.
previous_clause: Packets containing only PADDING frames therefore consume congestion window but do not generate acknowledgments that will open the congestion window.

target_clause: A client or server MAY advertise support for any of these reserved versions.
previous_clause: That is, any version number where the low four bits of all bytes is 1010 (in binary).
next_clause: Reserved version numbers will never represent a real protocol; a client MAY use one of these version numbers with the expectation that the server will initiate version negotiation; a server MAY advertise support for one of these versions and can expect that clients ignore the value.

target_clause: Unsupported parameters MUST be ignored.
previous_clause: The values in the SETTINGS frame MUST be processed in the order they appear, with no other frame processing between values.
next_clause: Once all values have been processed, the recipient MUST immediately emit a SETTINGS frame with the ACK flag set.

target_clause: If a sender receives a WINDOW_UPDATE that causes a flow-control window to exceed this maximum, it MUST terminate either the stream or the connection, as appropriate.
previous_clause: A sender MUST NOT allow a flow-control window to exceed 231-1 octets.
next_clause: For streams, the sender sends a RST_STREAM with an error code of FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR; for the connection, a GOAWAY frame with an error code of FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR is sent.

target_clause: An endpoint MUST initiate a key update ([key-update]) prior to exceeding any limit set for the AEAD that is in use.
previous_clause: This might be lower than the packet number limit.

next_clause: If an endpoint provided fewer connection IDs than the peer's active_connection_id_limit, it MAY supply a new connection ID when it receives a packet with a previously unused connection ID.

target_clause: An endpoint SHOULD limit the number of connection IDs it has retired locally and have not yet been acknowledged.
previous_clause: Failure to cease using the connection IDs when requested can result in connection failures, as the issuing endpoint might be unable to continue using the connection IDs with the active connection.
next_clause: An endpoint SHOULD allow for sending and tracking a number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames of at least twice the active_connection_id limit.

target_clause: An extension that changes existing elements MUST be negotiated before being used.
previous_clause: This includes changes to the layout of frames, additions or changes to the way that frames are composed into HTTP messages, the definition of pseudo-header fields, or changes to any protocol element that a compliant endpoint might treat as a connection error.
next_clause: For example, an extension that changes the layout of the HEADERS frame cannot be used until the peer has given a positive signal that this is acceptable.

target_clause: An endpoint SHOULD include new data in this packet.
previous_clause: When the PTO timer expires, an ack-eliciting packet MUST be sent.
next_clause: Previously sent data MAY be sent if no new data can be sent.

previous_clause: A receiver of RESET_STREAM can discard any data that it already received on that stream.
next_clause: The RESET_STREAM frame is as follows:

target_clause: Any given parameter MUST appear at most once in a given transport parameters extension.
previous_clause: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a transport parameter with an invalid value as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.
next_clause: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of duplicate transport parameters as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.

target_clause: RST_STREAM MUST be instigated by the application and MUST carry an application error code.
previous_clause: If stream 0 is closed with either a RST_STREAM or STREAM frame bearing the FIN flag, an endpoint MUST generate a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
next_clause: Resetting a stream without knowledge of the application protocol could cause the protocol to enter an unrecoverable state.

target_clause: Note that this mechanism does not protect against downgrade attacks and MUST NOT be used outside of draft implementations.
previous_clause: The new connection MUST use a new random Destination Connection ID different from the one it had previously sent.

target_clause: The content of a RST_STREAM frame MUST NOT change when it is sent again.
previous_clause: Cancellation of stream transmission, as carried in a RST_STREAM frame, is sent until acknowledged or until all stream data is acknowledged by the peer (that is, either the “Reset Recvd” or “Data Recvd” state is reached on the send stream).
next_clause: Similarly, a request to cancel stream transmission, as encoded in a STOP_SENDING frame, is sent until the receive stream enters either a “Data Recvd” or “Reset Recvd” state, see [solicited-state-transitions].

target_clause: Frames of unknown types ([extensions]), including reserved frames ([frame-reserved]) MAY be sent on a request or push stream before, after, or interleaved with other frames described in this section.
previous_clause: PUSH_PROMISE frames are not permitted on push streams; a pushed response that includes PUSH_PROMISE frames MUST be treated as a connection error of type H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED; see [errors].
next_clause: The HEADERS and PUSH_PROMISE frames might reference updates to the QPACK dynamic table.

target_clause: A HelloRetryRequest handshake message and any second ClientHello that is sent in response MUST also be sent without packet protection.
section_heading: Retransmission and Acknowledgment of Unprotected Packets
previous_clause: A HelloRetryRequest handshake message might be used to reject an initial ClientHello.
next_clause: This is natural, because no new keying material will be available when these messages need to be sent.

target_clause: Keys and their corresponding secrets SHOULD be discarded when an endpoint has received all packets with sequence numbers lower than the lowest sequence number used for the new key.
previous_clause: Packets with higher packet numbers always use the updated keys and MUST NOT be decrypted with old keys.
next_clause: An endpoint might discard keys if it determines that the length of the delay to affected packets is excessive.

target_clause: Streams SHOULD be used sequentially, with no gaps.
previous_clause: Streams which terminate abruptly may be reset at any point in the frame.
next_clause: HTTP does not need to do any separate multiplexing when using QUIC - data sent over a QUIC stream always maps to a particular HTTP transaction.

target_clause: Endpoints MUST NOT send Initial packets after this point.
previous_clause: Thus, a client MUST discard Initial keys when it first sends a Handshake packet and a server MUST discard Initial keys when it first successfully processes a Handshake packet.
next_clause: This results in abandoning loss recovery state for the Initial encryption level and ignoring any outstanding Initial packets.

target_clause: Once a final size for a stream is known, it cannot change. If a RESET_STREAM or STREAM frame is received indicating a change in the final size for the stream, an endpoint SHOULD respond with a FINAL_SIZE_ERROR error; see [error-handling].
previous_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT send data on a stream at or beyond the final size.
next_clause: A receiver SHOULD treat receipt of data at or beyond the final size as a FINAL_SIZE_ERROR error, even after a stream is closed.

target_clause: If the packet contains a version that is acceptable to the server, the server proceeds with the handshake (Section 6.2). All subsequent packets sent by the server MUST have the VERSION flag unset.
previous_clause: A server MUST send a version negotiation packet for every packet that it receives with an unacceptable version.
next_clause: This commits the server to the version that the client selected.

target_clause: The initiator of the close need not wait for the responding "close_notify" alert before closing the read side of the connection.
previous_clause: The other party MUST respond with a "close_notify" alert of its own and close down the connection immediately, discarding any pending writes.
next_clause: If the application protocol using TLS provides that any data may be carried over the underlying transport after the TLS connection is closed, the TLS implementation MUST receive the responding "close_notify" alert before indicating to the application layer that the TLS connection has ended.

target_clause: An implementation MAY use knowledge about application sending behavior or heuristics to determine whether and for how long to wait.
previous_clause: A sender MAY wait for a short period of time to collect multiple frames before sending a packet that is not maximally packed, to avoid sending out large numbers of small packets.
next_clause: This waiting period is an implementation decision, and an implementation should be careful to delay conservatively, since any delay is likely to increase application-visible latency.

target_clause: An endpoint SHOULD abandon path validation after sending some number of PATH_CHALLENGE frames or after some time has passed.
next_clause: When setting this timer, implementations are cautioned that the new path could have a longer round-trip time than the original.

target_clause: If an endpoint is no longer interested in the data being received, it MAY send a STOP_SENDING frame on a stream in the "open" or "half-closed (local)" state to prompt closure of the stream in the opposite direction.
next_clause: This typically indicates that the receiving application is no longer reading from the stream, but is not a guarantee that incoming data will be ignored.

target_clause: The client MAY use this value in place of its default for the initial RTT estimate.
previous_clause: The client MAY compute an RTT estimate to the server as the time period from when the first Initial was sent to when a Retry or a Version Negotiation packet is received.

target_clause: Streams MUST be created or reserved in sequential order, but MAY be used in arbitrary order.
previous_clause: StreamID 1 MUST NOT be used for application data, and MUST be the first client-initiated stream.
next_clause: A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a StreamID on a given connection.

target_clause: Implementations that detect spurious retransmissions and increase the reordering threshold in packets or time MAY choose to start with smaller initial reordering thresholds to minimize recovery latency.
previous_clause: Spuriously declaring packets as lost leads to unnecessary retransmissions and may result in degraded performance due to the actions of the congestion controller upon detecting loss.

target_clause: To improve efficiency and interoperability, field names MUST be converted to lowercase when constructing an HTTP/2 message.
previous_clause: HTTP fields (Section 5 of [HTTP]) are conveyed by HTTP/2 in the HEADERS, CONTINUATION, and PUSH_PROMISE frames, compressed with HPACK.

target_clause: An application protocol SHOULD provide guidance about the conditions under which generating a PING is recommended.
previous_clause: The PING frame can be used to keep a connection alive when an application or application protocol wishes to prevent the connection from timing out.
next_clause: This guidance SHOULD indicate whether it is the client or the server that is expected to send the PING.

target_clause: SETTINGS frames always apply to a connection, never a single stream, and MUST only be sent on the connection control stream (Stream 3).
previous_clause: An implementation MUST ignore the contents for any SETTINGS identifier it does not understand.
next_clause: If an endpoint receives an SETTINGS frame whose stream identifier field is anything other than 0x0, the endpoint MUST respond with a connection error of type HTTP_SETTINGS_ON_WRONG_STREAM.

target_clause: kMinRTOTimeout (RECOMMENDED 200ms):: Minimum time in the future an RTO timer may be set for.
previous_clause: kMinTLPTimeout (RECOMMENDED 10ms):: Minimum time in the future a tail loss probe timer may be set for.
next_clause: kDelayedAckTimeout (RECOMMENDED 25ms):: The length of the peer’s delayed ack timer.

target_clause: Servers MUST treat receipt of a NEW_TOKEN frame as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

previous_clause: The most appropriate error code ([error-codes]) SHOULD be included in the frame that signals the error.
next_clause: A stateless reset ([stateless-reset]) is not suitable for any error that can be signaled with a CONNECTION_CLOSE or RESET_STREAM frame.

target_clause: In this case, the client MUST apply the new settings immediately upon receipt.
previous_clause: Servers MAY continue processing data from clients which exceed its current configuration during the initial flight.
next_clause: When a 1-RTT QUIC connection is being used, the client MUST NOT send requests prior to receiving and processing the server’s SETTINGS frame.

target_clause: When sending data after becoming idle, a sender MUST reset its congestion window to the initial congestion window (see Section 4.1 of [RFC5681]), unless it paces the sending of packets.

previous_clause: A sender’s congestion window MUST NOT increase while it is idle.
next_clause: A sender MAY retain its congestion window if it paces the sending of any packets in excess of the initial congestion window.

next_clause: Due to network changes outside the control of its peer, an endpoint might receive packets from a new source address with the same destination connection ID, in which case it MAY continue to use the current connection ID with the new remote address while still sending from the same local address.

previous_clause: Consequently, a Version Negotiation packet consumes an entire UDP datagram.
next_clause: See [version-negotiation] for a description of the version negotiation process.

previous_clause: When a client resets a request with the error code HTTP_REQUEST_CANCELLED, a server MAY abruptly terminate the response using the error code HTTP_REQUEST_REJECTED if no processing was performed.

previous_clause: Handshake frames may be cancelled by handshake state transitions.
next_clause: When stateless rejects are in use, the connection is considered immediately closed once a reject is sent, so no timer is set to retransmit the reject.

previous_clause: A crash or outage might result in peers continuing to send data to an endpoint that is unable to properly continue the connection.
next_clause: A stateless reset is not appropriate for indicating errors in active connections.

next_clause: Providing a reference to any analysis upon which values are based - and any assumptions used in that analysis - allows limits to be adapted to varying usage conditions.

previous_clause: The codepoint of 0x00000000 is permanently reserved; the note for this codepoint [shall] indicate[s] that this version is reserved for Version Negotiation.

target_clause: A QUIC implementation SHOULD provide ways in which an application can indicate the relative priority of streams.
previous_clause: Instead, it relies on receiving priority information from the application.
next_clause: An implementation uses information provided by the application to determine how to allocate resources to active streams.

target_clause: Endpoints MUST NOT increase the value they send in the last stream identifier, since the peers might already have retried unprocessed requests on another connection.
previous_clause: The last stream identifier from the last GOAWAY frame received indicates which streams could have been acted upon.
next_clause: A client that is unable to retry requests loses all requests that are in flight when the server closes the connection.

target_clause: If the unacknowledged retransmittable packets are not acknowledged during this time, then these packets MUST be marked as lost.
previous_clause: If there are unacknowledged retransmittable packets still pending, they should be marked as lost. To compensate for the reduced reordering resilience, the sender SHOULD set an alarm for a small period of time.
next_clause: An endpoint SHOULD set the alarm such that a packet is marked as lost no earlier than 1.25 * max(SRTT, latest_RTT) since when it was sent.

target_clause: If a client receives packets from a new server address not indicated by the preferred_address transport parameter, the client SHOULD discard these packets.
previous_clause: Migrating a connection to a new server address mid-connection is left for future work.

target_clause: Endpoints MAY use other signals to detect that a peer has received the frames that caused stream to become "closed" and treat receipt of any frame other than PRIORITY as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
previous_clause: An endpoint can perform this minimal processing for all streams that are in the "closed" state.
next_clause: Endpoints can use frames that indicate that the peer has received the closing signal to drive this.

target_clause: A server MUST NOT use 0-RTT keys to protect anything other than TLS handshake messages.
previous_clause: This prevents stalling of the connection and allows the client to send continuously.
next_clause: Servers therefore treat packets protected with 0-RTT keys as equivalent to unprotected packets in determining what is permissible to send.

target_clause: However, the receiver MUST be prepared to receive data that exceeds this window size, since the sender might send data that exceeds the lower limit prior to processing the SETTINGS frame.

next_clause: After sending a SETTINGS frame that reduces the initial flow-control window size, a receiver MAY continue to process streams that exceed flow-control limits.

target_clause: Endpoints that limit the size of packets MAY use higher confidentiality and integrity limits; see [aead-analysis] for details.
previous_clause: Applying this limit reduces the probability that an attacker can successfully forge a packet; see [AEBounds], [ROBUST], and [GCM-MU].
next_clause: Future analyses and specifications MAY relax confidentiality or integrity limits for an AEAD.

target_clause: Even though newer keys could be available when retransmitting, retransmissions of these handshake messages MUST be sent in cleartext packets.
section_heading: Retransmission and Acknowledgment of Unprotected Packets
previous_clause: If these handshake messages are included in packets that are protected with these keys, they will be indecipherable to the recipient.
next_clause: An endpoint MUST generate ACK frames for these messages and send them in cleartext packets.

target_clause: A server MAY treat a packet that contains a different cryptographic handshake message as a connection error or discard it.
previous_clause: A client MUST use the same cryptographic handshake message it included in this packet.
next_clause: Note that including a Token field reduces the available space for the cryptographic handshake message, which might result in the client needing to send multiple Initial packets.

target_clause: QUIC extensions MUST describe how replay attacks affect their operation, or prohibit their use in 0-RTT.
previous_clause: Disabling 0-RTT entirely is the most effective defense against replay attack.
next_clause: Application protocols MUST either prohibit the use of extensions that carry application semantics in 0-RTT or provide replay mitigation strategies.

target_clause: After receiving a 1-RTT packet, servers MUST discard 0-RTT keys within a short time; the RECOMMENDED time period is three times the Probe Timeout (PTO, see [QUIC-RECOVERY]).
previous_clause: Servers MAY temporarily retain 0-RTT keys to allow decrypting reordered packets without requiring their contents to be retransmitted with 1-RTT keys.
next_clause: A server MAY discard 0-RTT keys earlier if it determines that it has received all 0-RTT packets, which can be done by keeping track of missing packet numbers.

target_clause: An endpoint MUST terminate a connection with a FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR error if it receives more data than the maximum data value that it has sent.
previous_clause: The sum of the final sizes on all streams - including streams in terminal states - MUST NOT exceed the value advertised by a receiver.
next_clause: This includes violations of remembered limits in Early Data; see [zerortt-parameters].

target_clause: If an endpoint receives a frame which corresponds to a stream which is allocated to it (i.e., odd-numbered for the client or even-numbered for the server) but which it has not yet created, it MUST close the connection with error code STREAM_STATE_ERROR.
previous_clause: To avoid Stream ID collision, clients MUST initiate streams using odd-numbered Stream IDs; servers MUST initiate streams using even-numbered Stream IDs.
next_clause: Stream ID 0 (0x0) is reserved for the cryptographic handshake.

target_clause: The stateless reset token MUST be difficult to guess.
next_clause: In order to create a Stateless Reset Token, an endpoint could randomly generate ([RANDOM]) a secret for every connection that it creates.

previous_clause: This only affects the establishment of HTTP/2 connections over cleartext TCP; HTTP/2 connections over TLS MUST use protocol negotiation in TLS.
next_clause: Without additional information, prior support for HTTP/2 is not a strong signal that a given server will support HTTP/2 for future connections.

target_clause: If the connection is closed because these or other constraints were violated during the 0-RTT flight (e.g. with HTTP_HPACK_DECOMPRESSION_FAILED), clients MAY establish a new connection and retry any 0-RTT requests using the settings sent by
previous_clause: In this case, the client MUST apply the new settings immediately upon receipt.
next_clause: the server on the closed connection.

target_clause: The receiver of coalesced QUIC packets MUST individually process each QUIC packet and separately acknowledge them, as if they were received as the payload of different UDP datagrams.
previous_clause: Every QUIC packet that is coalesced into a single UDP datagram is separate and complete.
next_clause: For example, if decryption fails (because the keys are not available or any other reason), the receiver MAY either discard or buffer the packet for later processing and MUST attempt to process the remaining packets.

target_clause: For a response only, a server MAY send any number of interim responses before the HEADERS frame containing a final response.

next_clause: An interim response consists of a HEADERS frame (which might be followed by zero or more CONTINUATION frames) containing the control data and header section of an interim (1xx) HTTP response (see Section 15 of [HTTP]).

target_clause: The peer SHOULD retire the corresponding connection IDs and send the corresponding RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames in a timely manner.
previous_clause: This includes the initial and preferred_address transport parameter connection IDs.
next_clause: The Retire Prior To field MUST be less than or equal to the Sequence Number field.

target_clause: Servers SHOULD ensure that tokens sent in Retry packets are only accepted for a short time.
previous_clause: To protect against such attacks, servers MUST ensure that replay of tokens is prevented or limited.
next_clause: Tokens that are provided in NEW_TOKEN frames ([frame-new-token]) need to be valid for longer, but SHOULD NOT be accepted multiple times in a short period.

target_clause: Endpoints SHOULD include at least one such setting in their SETTINGS frame.
previous_clause: Such settings have no defined meaning.
next_clause: Endpoints MUST NOT consider such settings to have any meaning upon receipt.

target_clause: A PRIORITY frame received after other frames on a request stream MUST be treated as a stream error of type HTTP_UNEXPECTED_FRAME.
previous_clause: In order to ensure that prioritization is processed in a consistent order, any subsequent PRIORITY frames for that request MUST be sent on the control stream.
next_clause: If, by the time a new request stream is opened, its priority information has already been received via the control stream, the PRIORITY frame sent on the request stream MUST be ignored.

target_clause: Any message containing connection-specific header fields MUST be treated as malformed.
previous_clause: This includes the Connection header field and those listed as having connection-specific semantics in Section 7.6.1 of [HTTP] (that is, Proxy-Connection, Keep-Alive, Transfer-Encoding, and Upgrade).
next_clause: The only exception to this is the TE header field, which MAY be present in an HTTP/2 request; when it is, it MUST NOT contain any value other than "trailers".

target_clause: The server MUST use consistent Source Connection IDs during the handshake.
previous_clause: The Destination Connection ID field in the server’s Initial packet contains a connection ID that is chosen by the recipient of the packet (i.e., the client); the Source Connection ID includes the connection ID that the sender of the packet wishes to use (see [connection-id]).
next_clause: On first receiving an Initial or Retry packet from the server, the client uses the Source Connection ID supplied by the server as the Destination Connection ID for subsequent packets, including any subsequent 0-RTT packets.

target_clause: Once TLS negotiation is complete, both the client and the server MUST send a connection preface.
previous_clause: The "h2c" protocol identifier MUST NOT be sent by a client or selected by a server; the "h2c" protocol identifier describes a protocol that does not use TLS.

target_clause: The server SHOULD also initiate path validation of the client using its preferred address and the address from which it received the client probe.
previous_clause: If this packet contains a PATH_CHALLENGE frame, the server sends a PATH_RESPONSE frame as per [migrate-validate]. The server MAY send other non-probing frames from its preferred address, but MUST continue sending all probing packets from its original IP address.
next_clause: This helps to guard against spurious migration initiated by an attacker.

target_clause: A client which wishes to break linkability upon changing networks MUST use the connection ID provided by the server as well as incrementing the packet sequence number by an externally unpredictable value computed as described in Section 7.6.1.1.
previous_clause: Connection IDs MUST be used in the order in which they are numbered.
next_clause: Packet number gaps are cumulative.

target_clause: If a connection terminates without a GOAWAY frame, clients MUST assume that any request which was sent, whether in whole or in part, might have been processed.
previous_clause: This might be due to an explicit closure by the peer, a transport-level error, or a change in network topology which interrupts connectivity.

target_clause: A HEADERS frame without the END_HEADERS flag set MUST be followed by a CONTINUATION frame for the same stream.
previous_clause: END_HEADERS (0x4):: When set, the END_HEADERS flag indicates that this frame contains an entire field block and is not followed by any CONTINUATION frames.
next_clause: A receiver MUST treat the receipt of any other type of frame or a frame on a different stream as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.

target_clause: When the server rejects a request without performing any application processing, it SHOULD abort its response stream with the error code H3_REQUEST_REJECTED.
previous_clause: When the client aborts reading a response, it indicates that this response is no longer of interest. Implementations SHOULD cancel requests by abruptly terminating any directions of a stream that are still open.
next_clause: In this context, "processed" means that some data from the stream was passed to some higher layer of software that might have taken some action as a result.

target_clause: Other cipher suites MUST define usage limits in order to be used with QUIC.
previous_clause: For the cipher suites mentioned in this document, the limits in Section 5.5 of [TLS13] apply.

target_clause: PRIORITY frames received by a client MUST be treated as a stream error of type HTTP_UNEXPECTED_FRAME.
previous_clause: A PRIORITY frame received on any stream other than a request or control stream MUST be treated as a connection error of type HTTP_WRONG_STREAM.

target_clause: A client MUST discard a Version Negotiation packet that lists the QUIC version selected by the client.
previous_clause: A client MUST discard any Version Negotiation packet if it has received and successfully processed any other packet, including an earlier Version Negotiation packet.

target_clause: To avoid being used for an amplication attack, such endpoints MUST limit the cumulative size of packets it sends to three times the cumulative size of the packets that are received and attributed to the connection.

target_clause: If the peer violates this requirement, the endpoint MUST either drop the incoming packets on that path without generating a stateless reset or proceed with path validation and allow the peer to migrate.
previous_clause: If the peer sent the disable_active_migration transport parameter, an endpoint also MUST NOT send packets (including probing packets; see [probing]) from a different local address to the address the peer used during the handshake, unless the endpoint has acted on a preferred_address transport parameter from the peer.
next_clause: Generating a stateless reset or closing the connection would allow third parties in the network to cause connections to close by spoofing or otherwise manipulating observed traffic.

target_clause: Clients MUST NOT assume that an HTTP/QUIC endpoint is authoritative for other origins without an explicit signal.
previous_clause: As required by [RFC7838], clients MUST check that the nominated server can present a valid certificate for the origin before considering it authoritative.
next_clause: A server that does not wish clients to reuse connections for a particular origin can indicate that it is not authoritative for a request by sending a 421 (Misdirected Request) status code in response to the request (see Section 9.1.2 of [RFC7540]).

target_clause: Endpoints SHOULD NOT allow connections or migration to a loopback address if the same service was previously available at a different interface or if the address was provided by a service at a non-loopback address.
previous_clause: Endpoints MAY prevent connection attempts or migration to a loopback address.
next_clause: Endpoints that depend on these capabilities could offer an option to disable these protections.

previous_clause: Upon receipt of a Public Reset packet that contains a valid proof, a client MUST tear down state associated with the connection.
next_clause: A Public Reset that does not contain a valid proof MUST be ignored.

target_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT initiate a key update prior to having confirmed the handshake ([handshake-confirmed]).
previous_clause: The endpoint toggles the value of the Key Phase bit and uses the updated key and IV to protect all subsequent packets.
next_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT initiate a subsequent key update unless it has received an acknowledgment for a packet that was sent protected with keys from the current key phase.

target_clause: If a promised server push is not needed by the client, the client SHOULD send a CANCEL_PUSH frame.
previous_clause: The client can use stream flow control (see section 4.1 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT]) to limit the amount of data a server may commit to the pushed stream.
next_clause: If the push stream is already open or opens after sending the CANCEL_PUSH frame, the client can abort reading the stream with an error code of H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED.

target_clause: A receiver MUST treat the receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE on a stream that is neither "open" nor "half-closed (local)" as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
previous_clause: Since PUSH_PROMISE reserves a stream, ignoring a PUSH_PROMISE frame causes the stream state to become indeterminate.
next_clause: However, an endpoint that has sent RST_STREAM on the associated stream MUST handle PUSH_PROMISE frames that might have been created before the RST_STREAM frame is received and processed.

target_clause: Similarly, a client MUST treat the selection of an incompatible application protocol by a server as a connection error of type 0x178.
previous_clause: The server MUST treat the inability to select a compatible application protocol as a connection error of type 0x178 (no_application_protocol).

target_clause: If the client received and processed a Retry packet, it validates that the original_connection_id transport parameter is present and correct; otherwise, it validates that the transport parameter is absent. A client MUST treat a failed validation as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.
previous_clause: If the server sends a Retry packet, it MUST include the value of the Original Destination Connection ID field of the Retry packet (that is, the Destination Connection ID field from the client’s first Initial packet) in the transport parameter.

target_clause: The server SHOULD send PUSH_PROMISE or DUPLICATE_PUSH frames prior to sending HEADERS or DATA frames that reference the promised responses.
previous_clause: Ordering of a PUSH_PROMISE or DUPLICATE_PUSH in relation to certain parts of the response is important.
next_clause: This reduces the chance that a client requests a resource that will be pushed by the server.

target_clause: A client MUST treat receipt of a GOAWAY frame containing a Stream ID of any other type as a connection error of type H3_ID_ERROR.
previous_clause: In the server to client direction, it carries a QUIC Stream ID for a client-initiated bidirectional stream encoded as a variable-length integer.
next_clause: In the client to server direction, the GOAWAY frame carries a Push ID encoded as a variable-length integer.

target_clause: Endpoints SHOULD create the HTTP control stream as well as the unidirectional streams required by mandatory extensions (such as the QPACK encoder and decoder streams) first, and then create additional streams as allowed by their peer.
previous_clause: Note that an endpoint is not required to grant additional credits to create more unidirectional streams if its peer consumes all the initial credits before creating the critical unidirectional streams.

Recipients of unknown stream types MAY abort reading of the stream with an error code of H3_STREAM_CREATION_ERROR or a reserved error code ([http-error-codes]), but MUST NOT consider such streams to be a connection error of any kind.

previous_clause: Receiving and verifying the TLS Finished message is critical in ensuring the integrity of the TLS handshake.

target_clause: A frame payload that contains additional bytes after the identified fields or a frame payload that terminates before the end of the identified fields MUST be treated as a connection error of type H3_FRAME_ERROR; see [errors].
previous_clause: Each frame's payload MUST contain exactly the fields identified in its description.
next_clause: In particular, redundant length encodings MUST be verified to be self-consistent; see [frame-parsing].

previous_clause: When the client has sent the "post_handshake_auth" extension (see Section 4.2.6), a server MAY request client authentication at any time after the handshake has completed by sending a CertificateRequest message.
next_clause: If the client chooses to authenticate, it MUST send Certificate, CertificateVerify, and Finished.

target_clause: A client that attempts to send 0-RTT data MUST remember all other transport parameters used by the server.
previous_clause: The client MUST use the server's new values in the handshake instead; if the server does not provide new values, the default value is used.
next_clause: The server can remember these transport parameters, or store an integrity-protected copy of the values in the ticket and recover the information when accepting 0-RTT data.

target_clause: Any request or response that contains a pseudo-header field that appears in a header field section after a regular header field MUST be treated as malformed ([malformed]).
previous_clause: All pseudo-header fields MUST appear in the header field section before regular header fields.

previous_clause: A receiver MUST treat the receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE on a stream that is neither "open" nor "half-closed (local)" as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
next_clause: A receiver MUST treat the receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE that promises an illegal stream identifier as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.

target_clause: An application protocol that uses QUIC MUST describe how the protocol uses 0-RTT and the measures that are employed to protect against replay attack.
previous_clause: Ultimately, the responsibility for managing the risks of replay attacks with 0-RTT lies with an application protocol.
next_clause: An analysis of replay risk needs to consider all QUIC protocol features that carry application semantics.

target_clause: The endpoint MAY continue sending ACK frames immediately on each subsequently received packet, but the endpoint SHOULD return to acknowledging every other packet within a period of 1/8 x RTT, unless more ack-eliciting packets are received out of order.
previous_clause: In order to assist loss detection at the sender, an endpoint SHOULD send an ACK frame immediately on receiving an ack-eliciting packet that is out of order.
next_clause: If every subsequent ack-eliciting packet arrives out of order, then an ACK frame SHOULD be sent immediately for every received ack-eliciting packet.

target_clause: A client MUST treat receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE with conflicting header field values for the same Push ID as a connection error of type HTTP_MALFORMED_PUSH_PROMISE.

next_clause: Allowing duplicate references to the same Push ID is primarily to reduce duplication caused by concurrent requests.

target_clause: Promised requests MUST be cacheable (see Section 4.2.3 of [RFC7231]), MUST be safe (see Section 4.2.1 of [RFC7231]), and MUST NOT include a request body.
previous_clause: The SETTINGS_ENABLE_PUSH setting can be set to 0 to indicate that server push is disabled.
next_clause: Clients that receive a promised request that is not cacheable, that is not known to be safe, or that indicates the presence of a request body MUST reset the promised stream with a stream error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.

target_clause: It is RECOMMENDED that implementations place limits on the total lifetime of such keying material; these limits should take into account the lifetime of the peer's certificate, the likelihood of intervening revocation, and the time since the peer's online CertificateVerify signature.
previous_clause: Note that in principle it is possible to continue issuing new tickets which indefinitely extend the lifetime of the keying material originally derived from an initial non-PSK handshake (which was most likely tied to the peer's certificate).

target_clause: An endpoint SHOULD NOT send a PATH_CHALLENGE more frequently than it would an Initial packet, ensuring that connection migration is no more load on a new path than establishing a new connection.
previous_clause: However, an endpoint SHOULD NOT send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in a single packet.
next_clause: The endpoint MUST use unpredictable data in every PATH_CHALLENGE frame so that it can associate the peer's response with the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE.

target_clause: Endpoints are not required to compare new values against all previous values, but a duplicate value MAY be treated as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
previous_clause: The same Stateless Reset Token MUST NOT be used for multiple connection IDs.
next_clause: Note that Stateless Reset packets do not have any cryptographic protection.

target_clause: TLS early data MAY be used to send requests, provided that the guidance in [RFC8470] is observed.
previous_clause: Unless the use of a new type of TLS message depends on an interaction with the application-layer protocol, that TLS message can be sent after the handshake completes.
next_clause: Clients send requests in early data assuming initial values for all server settings.

target_clause: If the endpoint does not have Handshake keys, or it is not certain that the peer has Handshake keys, it MAY send CONNECTION_CLOSE frames in an Initial packet.
previous_clause: Prior to connection establishment a peer might not have 1-RTT keys, so endpoints SHOULD send CONNECTION_CLOSE frames in a Handshake packet.
next_clause: If multiple packets are sent, they can be coalesced (see [packet-coalesce]) to facilitate retransmission.

target_clause: The PING frame SHOULD be used to keep a connection alive when a stream is open.
previous_clause: The receiver of a PING frame simply needs to acknowledge the packet containing this frame.
next_clause: The default is to send a PING frame after 15 seconds of quiescence.

target_clause: If a HEADERS frame is received on a control stream, the recipient MUST respond with a connection error ([errors]) of type H3_FRAME_UNEXPECTED.
previous_clause: HEADERS frames can only be sent on request or push streams.

target_clause: Because the latter cannot be differentiated from an attack, an endpoint MUST immediately terminate the connection if it detects this condition.
previous_clause: This is only possible if there is a key compromise and an attack, or if the peer is incorrectly reverting to use of old keys.
next_clause: In deciding when to update keys, endpoints MUST NOT exceed the limits for use of specific keys, as described in Section 5.5 of [TLS13].

target_clause: The packet number for sending MUST start at zero for the first packet sent and MUST increase by at least one after sending a packet.
previous_clause: Each endpoint maintains a separate packet number for sending and receiving.
next_clause: A QUIC endpoint MUST NOT reuse a packet number within the same connection (that is, under the same cryptographic keys).

target_clause: When the client aborts reading a response, it indicates that this response is no longer of interest. Implementations SHOULD cancel requests by abruptly terminating any directions of a stream that are still open.
previous_clause: Clients can cancel requests by resetting and aborting the request stream with an error code of H3_REQUEST_CANCELLED ([http-error-codes]).
next_clause: When the server rejects a request without performing any application processing, it SHOULD abort its response stream with the error code H3_REQUEST_REJECTED.

target_clause: Upon receipt of a HelloRetryRequest, a client SHOULD cease any transmission of 0-RTT data; 0-RTT data will only be discarded by any server that sends a HelloRetryRequest.
section_heading: Retransmission and Acknowledgment of Unprotected Packets
previous_clause: This is natural, because no shared secret will be available when these messages need to be sent.
next_clause: The packet type ensures that protected packets are clearly distinguished from unprotected packets.

target_clause: An endpoint SHOULD therefore include acknowledgments for unprotected and any packets protected with 0-RTT keys until it sees an acknowledgment for a packet that is both protected with 1-RTT keys and contains an "ACK" frame.
previous_clause: All "ACK" frames contained in unprotected packets that are received after successful receipt of a packet protected with 1-RTT keys MUST be discarded.

target_clause: The IPv6 flow label SHOULD be a pseudo-random function of the source and destination addresses, source and destination UDP ports, and the destination CID.
section_heading: Use of IPv6 Flow-Label and Migration
previous_clause: Endpoints that send data using IPv6 SHOULD apply an IPv6 flow label in compliance with [RFC6437], unless the local API does not allow setting IPv6 flow labels.
next_clause: The flow label generation MUST be designed to minimize the chances of linkability with a previously used flow label, as this would enable correlating activity on multiple paths; see [migration-linkability].

target_clause: Clients MUST NOT send new requests on the connection after receiving GOAWAY, although requests might already be in transit.
previous_clause: Once GOAWAY is sent, the server MUST reject requests sent on streams with an identifier greater than or equal to the indicated last Stream ID.
next_clause: A new connection can be established for new requests.

target_clause: A client MUST NOT change the cryptographic handshake message it sends in response to receiving a Retry.
previous_clause: A client MAY attempt 0-RTT after receiving a Retry packet by sending 0-RTT packets to the connection ID provided by the server.
next_clause: A client MUST NOT reset the packet number for any packet number space after processing a Retry packet.

target_clause: All curves currently specified in this document MUST only be used with the uncompressed point format (the format for all ECDH functions is considered uncompressed).
previous_clause: Although X9.62 supports multiple point formats, any given curve MUST specify only a single point format.
next_clause: For x25519 and x448, the contents are the byte string inputs and outputs of the corresponding functions defined in [RFC7748], 32 bytes for x25519 and 56 bytes for x448.

target_clause: Implementations MUST ignore unknown or unsupported values in all extensible protocol elements.
previous_clause: Registries are established for managing these extension points: frame types ([iana-frames]), settings ([iana-settings]), error codes ([iana-error-codes]), and stream types ([iana-stream-types]).
next_clause: Implementations MUST discard frames and abort reading on unidirectional streams that have unknown or unsupported types.

target_clause: QUIC endpoints that implement any kind of PMTU discovery SHOULD maintain an estimate for each combination of local and remote IP addresses (as each pairing could have a different maximum MTU in the path).
previous_clause: Assuming the minimum IP header size, this results in a QUIC packet size of 1232 octets for IPv6 and 1252 octets for IPv4.
next_clause: QUIC depends on the network path supporting a MTU of at least 1280 octets.

target_clause: If an endpoint receives a SETTINGS frame whose stream identifier field is anything other than 0x0, the endpoint MUST respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
previous_clause: The stream identifier for a SETTINGS frame MUST be zero (0x0).
next_clause: The SETTINGS frame affects connection state.

target_clause: A client MUST abort a connection if the server picks an incompatible combination of QUIC version and ALPN identifier.
previous_clause: If the server cannot select a compatible combination of application protocol and QUIC version, it MUST abort the connection.

target_clause: A CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1d MUST be replaced by a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1c when sending the frame in Initial or Handshake packets.
previous_clause: Sending a CONNECTION_CLOSE of type 0x1d in an Initial or Handshake packet could expose application state or be used to alter application state.
next_clause: Otherwise, information about the application state might be revealed.

target_clause: ACK frames SHOULD always acknowledge the most recently received packets, and the more out-of-order the packets are, the more important it is to send an updated ACK frame quickly, to prevent the peer from declaring a packet as lost and spuriously retransmitting the frames it contains.
previous_clause: Including acknowledgments for older packets reduces the chance of spurious retransmissions caused by losing previously sent ACK frames, at the cost of larger ACK frames.
next_clause: An ACK frame is expected to fit within a single QUIC packet.

target_clause: To ensure that packets can be both sent to and received from the peer, the PATH_RESPONSE MUST be sent on the same path as the triggering PATH_CHALLENGE: from the same local address on which the PATH_CHALLENGE was received, to the same remote address from which the PATH_CHALLENGE was received.
previous_clause: Since a PATH_CHALLENGE might be sent from a spoofed address, an endpoint MAY limit the rate at which it sends PATH_RESPONSE frames and MAY silently discard PATH_CHALLENGE frames that would cause it to respond at a higher rate.

target_clause: Streams used for pushed resources MAY be initiated out-of-order, but stream IDs SHOULD be allocated to promised resources sequentially.
previous_clause: Streams SHOULD be used sequentially, with no gaps.
next_clause: HTTP does not need to do any separate multiplexing when using QUIC - data sent over a QUIC stream always maps to a particular HTTP transaction.

target_clause: Servers that retain an open socket for accepting new connections SHOULD NOT end the closing or draining states early.
previous_clause: Endpoints that have some alternative means to ensure that late-arriving packets do not induce a response, such as those that are able to close the UDP socket, MAY end these states earlier to allow for faster resource recovery.
next_clause: Once its closing or draining state ends, an endpoint SHOULD discard all connection state.

target_clause: When multiple versions are supported, the "quic" parameter MAY be repeated multiple times in a single Alt-Svc entry.
previous_clause: Leading zeros SHOULD be omitted for brevity.
next_clause: For example, if a server supported both version 0x00000001 and the version rendered in ASCII as "Q034", it could specify the following header:

target_clause: A client that sends additional 0-RTT packets MUST NOT reset the packet number to 0 as a result, see [retry-0rtt-pn].
previous_clause: A client MAY attempt 0-RTT after receiving a Version Negotiation packet.
next_clause: Version negotiation packets have no cryptographic protection.

target_clause: The PSK used to encrypt the early data MUST be the first PSK listed in the client's "pre_shared_key" extension.
previous_clause: The parameters for the 0-RTT data (symmetric cipher suite, ALPN protocol, etc.) are the same as those which were negotiated in the connection which established the PSK.
next_clause: For PSKs provisioned via NewSessionTicket, a server MUST validate that the ticket age for the selected PSK identity (computed by subtracting ticket_age_add from PskIdentity.obfuscated_ticket_age modulo 2^32) is within a small tolerance of the time since the ticket was issued (see Section 8).

target_clause: The client MUST include the token in all Initial packets it sends, unless a Retry or NEW_TOKEN frame replaces the token with a newer one.
previous_clause: The client includes this token in Initial packets to provide address validation in a future connection.
next_clause: The client MUST NOT use the token provided in a Retry for future connections.

target_clause: Resumed connections over the same network SHOULD use the previous connection's final smoothed RTT value as the resumed connection's initial RTT.
previous_clause: The initial probe timeout for a new connection or new path SHOULD be set to twice the initial RTT.
next_clause: If no previous RTT is available, the initial RTT SHOULD be set to 500ms, resulting in a 1 second initial timeout as recommended in [RFC6298].

target_clause: However, endpoints SHOULD include buffering delays caused by unavailability of decryption keys, since these delays can be large and are likely to be non-repeating.
previous_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT include delays that it does not control when populating the ACK Delay field in an ACK frame.
next_clause: When the measured acknowledgment delay is larger than its max_ack_delay, an endpoint SHOULD report the measured delay.

target_clause: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint is unable to buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY discard that CRYPTO frame and all CRYPTO frames received in the future, or it MAY close the connection with an CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.
previous_clause: If an endpoint’s buffer is exceeded during the handshake, it can expand its buffer temporarily to complete the handshake. If an endpoint does not expand its buffer, it MUST close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.
next_clause: Packets containing discarded CRYPTO frames MUST be acknowledged because the packet has been received and processed by the transport even though the CRYPTO frame was discarded.

target_clause: - Implementations that advertise support for RSASSA-PSS (which is mandatory in TLS 1.3), MUST be prepared to accept a signature using that scheme even when TLS 1.2 is negotiated.
previous_clause: If TLS 1.2 is negotiated, implementations MUST be prepared to accept a signature that uses any curve that they advertised in the "supported_groups" extension.
next_clause: In TLS 1.2, RSASSA-PSS is used with RSA cipher suites.

target_clause: A client MUST accept and process at most one Retry packet for each connection attempt.
next_clause: After the client has received and processed an Initial or Retry packet from the server, it MUST discard any subsequent Retry packets that it receives.

target_clause: ACK frames MUST only be carried in a packet that has the same packet number space as the packet being acknowledged; see [packet-protected].
next_clause: For instance, packets that are protected with 1-RTT keys MUST be acknowledged in packets that are also protected with 1-RTT keys.

target_clause: Receivers MAY also limit ACK frame size further to preserve space for other frames or to limit the capacity that acknowledgments consume.
previous_clause: This is necessary if an ACK frame would be too large to fit in a packet.
next_clause: A receiver MUST retain an ACK Range unless it can ensure that it will not subsequently accept packets with numbers in that range.

target_clause: It is RECOMMENDED that endpoints immediately close the connection with a connection error of type AEAD_LIMIT_REACHED before reaching a state where key updates are not possible.
previous_clause: If a key update is not possible or integrity limits are reached, the endpoint MUST stop using the connection and only send stateless resets in response to receiving packets.
next_clause: For AEAD_AES_128_GCM and AEAD_AES_256_GCM, the confidentiality limit is 2^23 encrypted packets; see [gcm-bounds].

target_clause: The PTO timer MUST NOT be set if a timer is set for time threshold loss detection; see [time-threshold].
previous_clause: The total length of time over which consecutive PTOs expire is limited by the idle timeout.
next_clause: A timer that is set for time threshold loss detection will expire earlier than the PTO timer in most cases and is less likely to spuriously retransmit data.

target_clause: If the content of a PATH_RESPONSE frame does not match the content of a PATH_CHALLENGE frame previously sent by the endpoint, the endpoint MAY generate a connection error of type UNSOLICITED_PATH_RESPONSE.
previous_clause: Its format is identical to the PATH_CHALLENGE frame ([frame-path-challenge]).

target_clause: An endpoint MUST open streams of the same type in increasing order of stream ID.
previous_clause: The conditions for opening a stream are slightly more complex for a bidirectional stream because the opening of either the send or receive side causes the stream to open in both directions.
next_clause: Note:: These states are largely informative.

target_clause: The receiver MAY instead send a RST_STREAM with an error code of FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR for the affected streams.
previous_clause: Progress on these streams can also stall, since WINDOW_UPDATE frames are needed to allow the sender to resume sending.

target_clause: All other frame types MUST only be sent in the 0-RTT and 1-RTT levels.
previous_clause: ACK frames MAY appear in packets of any encryption level other than 0-RTT, but can only acknowledge packets which appeared in that packet number space.
next_clause: Note that it is not possible to send the following frames in 0-RTT for various reasons: ACK, CRYPTO, HANDSHAKE_DONE, NEW_TOKEN, PATH_RESPONSE, and RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID.

target_clause: Endpoints SHOULD abandon path validation based on a timer.
previous_clause: Path validation only fails when the endpoint attempting to validate the path abandons its attempt to validate the path.
next_clause: When setting this timer, implementations are cautioned that the new path could have a longer round-trip time than the original. A value of three times the larger of the current Probe Timeout (PTO) or the PTO for the new path (that is, using kInitialRtt as defined in [QUIC-RECOVERY]) is RECOMMENDED.

target_clause: A receiver MUST not send timestamps in unprotected packets.
previous_clause: A receiver MAY send timestamps for non-retransmittable packets.
next_clause: A sender MAY intentionally skip packet numbers to introduce entropy into the connection, to avoid opportunistic acknowledgement attacks.

target_clause: To avoid this, endpoints MUST either limit transmission of CONNECTION_CLOSE frames to validated addresses or drop packets without response if the response would be more than three times larger than the received packet.
previous_clause: New packets from unverified addresses could be used to create an amplification attack; see [address-validation].
next_clause: After receiving a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame, endpoints enter the draining state.

target_clause: A receiver MAY use an autotuning mechanism to tune the frequency and amount of advertised additional credit based on a round-trip time estimate and the rate at which the receiving application consumes data, similar to common TCP implementations.
previous_clause: Thus there is a trade-off between resource commitment and overhead when determining how large a limit is advertised.
next_clause: If a sender runs out of flow control credit, it will be unable to send new data and is considered blocked.

target_clause: If the number of packets that fail authentication with the same key exceeds a limit that is specific to the AEAD in use, the endpoint MUST stop using those keys.
previous_clause: Endpoints MUST count the number of received packets that fail authentication for each set of keys.
next_clause: Endpoints MUST initiate a key update before reaching this limit.

target_clause: The packet with the highest packet number MUST be used to determine which path to use.
previous_clause: Due to variations in path latency or packet reordering, packets from different source addresses might be reordered.
next_clause: Endpoints also need to be prepared to receive packets from an older source address.

target_clause: Endpoints MAY instead defer the creation of the next set of receive packet protection keys until some time after a key update completes, up to three times the PTO; see [old-keys-recv].
previous_clause: An endpoint MAY perform this process as part of packet processing, but this creates a timing signal that can be used by an attacker to learn when key updates happen and thus the value of the Key Phase bit in certain packets.
next_clause: Once generated, the next set of packet protection keys SHOULD be retained, even if the packet that was received was subsequently discarded.

target_clause: As the AEAD on Initial packets does not provide strong authentication, an endpoint MAY discard an invalid Initial packet.
previous_clause: The only mechanism available to an endpoint that continues to receive data for a terminated connection is to attempt the stateless reset process ([stateless-reset]).
next_clause: Discarding an Initial packet is permitted even where this specification otherwise mandates a connection error.

target_clause: Once an endpoint successfully receives a packet with a given packet number, it MUST discard all packets with higher packet numbers if they cannot be successfully unprotected with either the same key, or - if there is a key update - the next packet protection key (see [key-update]).
next_clause: Similarly, a packet that appears to trigger a key update, but cannot be unprotected successfully MUST be discarded.

target_clause: Receipt of a frame that permits opening of a stream larger than this limit MUST be treated as a FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR.
previous_clause: This value cannot exceed 2^60, as it is not possible to encode stream IDs larger than 2^62-1.
next_clause: Loss or reordering can cause a MAX_STREAMS frame to be received that state a lower stream limit than an endpoint has previously received.

target_clause: Upon receipt, the peer MUST first retire the corresponding connection IDs using RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames and then add the newly provided connection ID to the set of active connection IDs.
previous_clause: An endpoint can cause its peer to retire connection IDs by sending a NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame with an increased Retire Prior To field.
next_clause: Failure to retire the connection IDs within approximately one PTO can cause packets to be delayed, lost, or cause the original endpoint to send a stateless reset in response to a connection ID it can no longer route correctly.

target_clause: Clients MUST NOT cache session tickets for longer than 7 days, regardless of the ticket_lifetime.
previous_clause: The value of zero indicates that the ticket should be discarded immediately.
next_clause: It MAY delete the ticket earlier based on local policy.

target_clause: A PRIORITY frame received on any stream other than a request or control stream MUST be treated as a connection error of type HTTP_WRONG_STREAM.
previous_clause: A PRIORITY frame that references a non-existent Push ID, a Placeholder ID greater than the server’s limit, or a Stream ID the client is not yet permitted to open MUST be treated as an HTTP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED error.
next_clause: PRIORITY frames received by a client MUST be treated as a connection error of type HTTP_UNEXPECTED_FRAME.

target_clause: A server MAY use the same Push ID in multiple PUSH_PROMISE frames.
previous_clause: A client MUST treat receipt of a PUSH_PROMISE frame that contains a larger Push ID than the client has advertised as a connection error of H3_ID_ERROR.
next_clause: If so, the decompressed request header sets MUST contain the same fields in the same order, and both the name and the value in each field MUST be exact matches.

target_clause: A server MUST include the original_connection_id transport parameter if it sent a Retry packet.
previous_clause: This is the same value sent in the "Original Destination Connection ID" field of a Retry packet (see [packet-retry]).
next_clause: max_idle_timeout (0x01):: The max idle timeout is a value in milliseconds that is encoded as an integer; see ([idle-timeout]).
