target_clause: A client MUST authenticate the identity of the server.
previous_clause: TLS provides server authentication and permits the server to request client authentication.
next_clause: This typically involves verification that the identity of the server is included in a certificate and that the certificate is issued by a trusted entity (see for example [RFC2818]).

target_clause: To fulfill this privacy requirement, endpoints that initiate migration and use connection IDs with length greater than zero SHOULD provide their peers with new connection IDs before migration.
previous_clause: The goal here is to ensure that packets sent on different paths cannot be correlated.
next_clause: Caution:: If both endpoints change connection ID in response to seeing a change in connection ID from their peer, then this can trigger an infinite sequence of changes.

target_clause: Correspondingly, a proxy MUST send a TCP segment with the RST bit set if it detects an error with the stream or the QUIC connection.
previous_clause: A proxy treats any error in the TCP connection, which includes receiving a TCP segment with the RST bit set, as a stream error of type HTTP_CONNECT_ERROR ([http-error-codes]).

target_clause: Version negotiation packets are always stateless, and MUST be sent once per handshake packet that uses an unsupported QUIC version, and MAY be sent in response to 0RTT packets.
previous_clause: When stateless rejects are in use, the connection is considered immediately closed once a reject is sent, so no timer is set to retransmit the reject.

target_clause: Servers MAY also reject requests on streams below the indicated ID if these requests were not processed.
previous_clause: If the client has sent requests on streams with a Stream ID greater than or equal to that indicated in the GOAWAY frame, those requests are considered rejected ([request-cancellation]). Clients SHOULD cancel any requests on streams above this ID.
next_clause: Requests on Stream IDs less than the Stream ID in the GOAWAY frame might have been processed; their status cannot be known until they are completed successfully, reset individually, or the connection terminates.

target_clause: A QUIC stack that chooses to support the spin bit MUST implement it as specified in this section.
previous_clause: The spin bit is an OPTIONAL feature of this version of QUIC.
next_clause: Each endpoint unilaterally decides if the spin bit is enabled or disabled for a connection.

previous_clause: All other values are assigned to Private Use [RFC8126].
next_clause: Value:: The numeric value of the assignment (registrations will be between 0x00 and 0x3fff).

target_clause: When the measured acknowledgement delay is larger than its max_ack_delay, an endpoint SHOULD report the measured delay.
previous_clause: However, endpoints SHOULD include buffering delays caused by unavailability of decryption keys, since these delays can be large and are likely to be non-repeating.
next_clause: This information is especially useful during the handshake when delays might be large; see [sending-acknowledgements].

target_clause: Servers MUST NOT use any value more than 604800 seconds (7 days).
previous_clause: ticket_lifetime Indicates the lifetime in seconds as a 32-bit unsigned integer in network byte order from the time of ticket issuance.
next_clause: The value of zero indicates that the ticket should be discarded immediately.

previous_clause: This length is encoded as a 8-bit unsigned integer.
next_clause: Endpoints that receive a version 1 long header with a value larger than 20 MUST drop the packet.

target_clause: If a max_streams transport parameter or a MAX_STREAMS frame is received with a value greater than 2^60, this would allow a maximum stream ID that cannot be expressed as a variable-length integer; see [integer-encoding]. If either is received, the connection MUST be closed immediately with a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR if the offending value was received in a transport parameter or of type FRAME_ENCODING_ERROR if it was received in a frame; see [immediate-close].
previous_clause: Separate limits apply to unidirectional and bidirectional streams.
next_clause: Endpoints MUST NOT exceed the limit set by their peer.

target_clause: If the maximum datagram size is decreased in order to complete the handshake, the congestion window SHOULD be set to the new initial congestion window.
previous_clause: If the maximum datagram size changes during the connection, the initial congestion window SHOULD be recalculated with the new size.
next_clause: Prior to validating the client's address, the server can be further limited by the anti-amplification limit as specified in Section 8.1 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT].

target_clause: An endpoint MAY send multiple GOAWAY frames if circumstances change.
previous_clause: If a connection terminates without a GOAWAY frame, the last Stream ID is effectively the highest possible Stream ID (as determined by QUIC’s MAX_STREAM_ID).
next_clause: For instance, an endpoint that sends GOAWAY without an error code during graceful shutdown could subsequently encounter an error condition.

target_clause: Senders MUST either use pacing or limit such bursts.
previous_clause: Sending multiple packets into the network without any delay between them creates a packet burst that might cause short-term congestion and losses.
next_clause: Senders SHOULD limit bursts to the initial congestion window; see [initial-cwnd].

target_clause: The TLS implementation MUST support the Server Name Indication (SNI) extension to TLS.
previous_clause: The general TLS usage guidance in [TLSBCP] SHOULD be followed, with some additional restrictions that are specific to HTTP/2.
next_clause: If the server is identified by a domain name, clients MUST send the server_name TLS extension unless an alternative mechanism to indicate the target host is used.

next_clause: ACK frames MAY appear in packets of any encryption level other than 0-RTT, but can only acknowledge packets which appeared in that packet number space.

target_clause: A sender SHOULD send a DATA_BLOCKED frame (type=0x14) when it wishes to send data, but is unable to do so due to connection-level flow control; see [flow-control].

target_clause: A receiver MAY also advance the maximum stream ID based on current activity, system conditions, and other environmental factors.

next_clause: Only idempotent actions such as GET, PUT, or DELETE can be safely retried; a client SHOULD NOT automatically retry a request with a non-idempotent method unless it has some means to know that the request semantics are idempotent independent of the method or some means to detect that the original request was never applied.

target_clause: Any further changes to the Destination Connection ID are only permitted if the values are taken from any received NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames; if subsequent Initial packets include a different Source Connection ID, they MUST be discarded.

next_clause: This avoids unpredictable outcomes that might otherwise result from stateless processing of multiple Initial packets with different Source Connection IDs.

target_clause: Stream 0 MUST NOT be used for application data, and is the first client-initiated stream.

next_clause: Like Initial packets (see [discard-initial]), data in CRYPTO frames for Handshake packets is discarded - and no longer retransmitted - when Handshake protection keys are discarded.

target_clause: When ack-eliciting packets in multiple packet number spaces are in flight, the timer MUST be set for the packet number space with the earliest timeout, with one exception.

next_clause: The ApplicationData packet number space (Section 4.1.1 of [QUIC-TLS]) MUST be ignored until the handshake completes.

target_clause: After allowing time for any in-flight requests (at least one round-trip time), the server MAY send another GOAWAY frame with an updated last Stream ID.

next_clause: This ensures that a connection can be cleanly shut down without losing requests.

target_clause: An endpoint MAY skip packet numbers when sending packets to detect this behavior.

next_clause: An endpoint can then immediately close the connection with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION; see [immediate-close].

previous_clause: Note that a request or response without a body will cause this stream to be half-closed in the corresponding direction without transferring data.
next_clause: If an implementation chooses to reject a request with a QUIC error code, it MUST trigger a QUIC RST_STREAM on the data stream only.

target_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT initiate connection migration before the handshake is finished and the endpoint has 1-RTT keys.
previous_clause: This section describes the process by which an endpoint migrates to a new address.
next_clause: The design of QUIC relies on endpoints retaining a stable address for the duration of the handshake.

target_clause: To ensure that the HTTP/1.1 request line can be reproduced accurately, this pseudo-header field MUST be omitted when translating from an HTTP/1.1 request that has a request target in origin or asterisk form (see Section 5.3 of [RFC7230]).
previous_clause: The authority MUST NOT include the deprecated userinfo subcomponent for http or https schemed URIs.

target_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT generate an HTTP/3 message containing connection-specific header fields; any message containing connection-specific header fields MUST be treated as malformed ([malformed]).

target_clause: A client MUST treat the receipt of a MAX_PUSH_ID frame as a connection error of type HTTP_FRAME_UNEXPECTED.
previous_clause: A server MUST NOT send a MAX_PUSH_ID frame.
next_clause: The maximum Push ID is unset when a connection is created, meaning that a server cannot push until it receives a MAX_PUSH_ID frame.

target_clause: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of a transport parameter with an invalid value as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.
previous_clause: Definitions for each of the defined transport parameters are included in [transport-parameter-definitions].
next_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT send a parameter more than once in a given transport parameters extension.

target_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT send more than one ACK-frame-only packet in response to receiving an ACK-eliciting packet (one containing frames other than ACK and/or PADDING).
previous_clause: Packets containing only ACK frames are not congestion controlled, so there are limits on how frequently they can be sent.
next_clause: An endpoint MUST NOT send a packet containing only an ACK frame in response to a non-ACK-eliciting packet (one containing only ACK and/or PADDING frames), even if there are packet gaps which precede the received packet.

target_clause: An endpoint that receives a STREAM frame for a send-only stream MUST terminate the connection with error PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.

target_clause: Frames received after a peer closes a stream SHOULD be discarded.
previous_clause: Due to reordering, an endpoint could continue receiving frames for the stream even after the stream is closed for sending.
next_clause: An endpoint MAY choose to limit the period over which it ignores frames and treat frames that arrive after this time as being in error.

target_clause: For path validation to be successful, a PATH_RESPONSE frame MUST be received from the same remote address to which the corresponding PATH_CHALLENGE was sent.
previous_clause: Receipt of an acknowledgment for a packet containing a PATH_CHALLENGE frame is not adequate validation, since the acknowledgment can be spoofed by a malicious peer.
next_clause: If a PATH_RESPONSE frame is received from a different remote address than the one to which the PATH_CHALLENGE was sent, path validation is considered to have failed, even if the data matches that sent in the PATH_CHALLENGE.

target_clause: An endpoint SHOULD use DPLPMTUD ([dplpmtud]) or PMTUD ([pmtud]) to determine whether the path to a destination will support a desired maximum datagram size without fragmentation.
previous_clause: The largest UDP payload an endpoint sends at any given time is referred to as the endpoint's maximum datagram size.
next_clause: In the absence of these mechanisms, QUIC endpoints SHOULD NOT send datagrams larger than the smallest allowed maximum datagram size.

target_clause: Specifically, the client MUST send an Initial packet in a UDP datagram of at least 1200 bytes if it does not have Handshake keys, and otherwise send a Handshake packet.
previous_clause: To prevent this deadlock, clients MUST send a packet on a probe timeout (PTO, see Section 5.3 of [QUIC-RECOVERY]).
next_clause: A server might wish to validate the client address before starting the cryptographic handshake.

target_clause: In this state, endpoints can send MAX_STREAM_DATA and MUST observe the value advertised by its receiving peer (see Section 11).
previous_clause: A stream in the "open" state may be used by both peers to send frames of any type.
next_clause: Opening a stream causes all lower-numbered streams in the same direction to become open.

target_clause: All implementations MUST be capable of receiving and minimally processing frames up to 214 octets in length, plus the 9-octet frame header.
previous_clause: This setting can have any value between 214 (16,384) and 224-1 (16,777,215) octets, inclusive.
next_clause: The size of the frame header is not included when describing frame sizes.

target_clause: If no use of the codepoint was identified and no request was made to update the registration, the codepoint MAY be removed from the registry.
previous_clause: A note might be added for the registration recording relevant information that was learned.

target_clause: Once this timer expires, an endpoint MUST NOT either accept or generate new packets using those packet protection keys.
previous_clause: These packets MAY also include PADDING frames.

target_clause: An implementation MUST ensure that the length of a frame exactly matches the length of the fields it contains.
previous_clause: This could pose a security risk to an incautious implementer.

target_clause: There are certain operations which an application MUST be able to perform when interacting with QUIC streams.
next_clause: This document does not specify an API, but any implementation of this version of QUIC MUST expose the ability to perform the operations described in this section on a QUIC stream.

target_clause: The most recent MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a stream MUST be retransmitted.
previous_clause: See [solicited-state-transitions].
next_clause: Any previous unacknowledged MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for the same stream SHOULD NOT be retransmitted since a newer MAX_STREAM_DATA frame for a stream obviates the need for delivering older ones.

target_clause: Tokens sent in Retry packets SHOULD include information that allows the server to verify that the source IP address and port in client packets remains constant.
previous_clause: There is no need for a single well-defined format for the token because the server that generates the token also consumes it.
next_clause: Tokens sent in NEW_TOKEN frames MUST include information that allows the server to verify that the client IP address has not changed from when the token was issued.

target_clause: In addition to the advice in [iana-policy], specifications for new permanent registrations SHOULD describe the means by which an endpoint might determine that it can send the identified type of frame.
previous_clause: Frame Name:: A short mnemonic for the frame type.
next_clause: An accompanying transport parameter registration is expected for most registrations; see [iana-transport-parameters].

target_clause: A sender MUST however count these packets as being additionally in flight, since these packets add network load without establishing packet loss.
previous_clause: Probe packets MUST NOT be blocked by the congestion controller.

target_clause: All other values MUST be ignored when processing a packet that contains an unsupported version.
previous_clause: o the Version (or Supported Versions, Section 5.3) field.

previous_clause: However, an endpoint SHOULD NOT send multiple PATH_CHALLENGE frames in a single packet.
next_clause: This ensures that connection migration is no more load on a new path than establishing a new connection.

target_clause: Since network congestion is not affected by packet number spaces, persistent congestion SHOULD consider packets sent across packet number spaces.
previous_clause: Requiring a prior RTT sample prevents a sender from establishing persistent congestion with potentially too few probes.
next_clause: A sender that does not have state for all packet number spaces or an implementation that cannot compare send times across packet number spaces MAY use state for just the packet number space that was acknowledged.

target_clause: All pseudo-header fields MUST appear in the header field section before regular header fields.
previous_clause: Endpoints MUST treat a request or response that contains undefined or invalid pseudo-header fields as malformed ([malformed]).
next_clause: Any request or response that contains a pseudo-header field that appears in a header field section after a regular header field MUST be treated as malformed ([malformed]).

target_clause: Description:: A brief description of the error code semantics, which MAY be a summary if a specification reference is provided.
previous_clause: Code:: A short mnemonic for the parameter.
next_clause: The initial contents of this registry are shown in [iana-error-table].

target_clause: A client MUST NOT send 0-RTT packets once it starts processing 1-RTT packets from the server.
previous_clause: A client only receives acknowledgments for its 0-RTT packets once the handshake is complete, as defined in Section 4.1.1 of [QUIC-TLS].
next_clause: This means that 0-RTT packets cannot contain any response to frames from 1-RTT packets.

target_clause: Clients SHOULD NOT wait indefinitely for SETTINGS to arrive before sending requests, but SHOULD process received datagrams in order to increase the likelihood of processing SETTINGS before sending the first request.
previous_clause: 1-RTT keys will always become available prior to the packet containing SETTINGS being processed by QUIC, even if the server sends SETTINGS immediately.
next_clause: When a 0-RTT QUIC connection is being used, the initial value of each server setting is the value used in the previous session. Clients SHOULD store the settings the server provided in the HTTP/3 connection where resumption information was provided, but MAY opt not to store settings in certain cases (e.g., if the session ticket is received before the SETTINGS frame).

target_clause: Endpoints MAY re-establish the min_rtt at other times in the connection, such as when traffic volume is low and an acknowledgment is received with a low acknowledgment delay.
previous_clause: This is to allow a connection to reset its estimate of min_rtt and smoothed_rtt ([smoothed-rtt]) after a disruptive network event, and because it is possible that an increase in path delay resulted in persistent congestion being incorrectly declared.
next_clause: Implementations SHOULD NOT refresh the min_rtt value too often, since the actual minimum RTT of the path is not frequently observable.

target_clause: If a promised server push is not needed by the client, the client SHOULD send a CANCEL_PUSH frame; if the push stream is already open, a QUIC STOP_SENDING frame with an appropriate error code can be used instead (e.g., HTTP_PUSH_REFUSED, HTTP_PUSH_ALREADY_IN_CACHE; see [errors]).
previous_clause: Ordering of a PUSH_PROMISE in relation to certain parts of the response is important (see Section 8.2.1 of [RFC7540]).

previous_clause: Permanent registrations in this registry are assigned using the Specification Required policy ([RFC8126]), except for values between 0x00 and 0x3f (in hexadecimal; inclusive), which are assigned using Standards Action or IESG Approval as defined in Section 4.9 and 4.10 of [RFC8126].
next_clause: Frame Name:: A short mnemonic for the frame type.

target_clause: After sending the GOAWAY frame for an error condition, the endpoint MUST close the TCP connection.
previous_clause: The GOAWAY frame includes an error code that indicates why the connection is terminating.
next_clause: It is possible that the GOAWAY will not be reliably received by the receiving endpoint.

target_clause: A server that wishes to communicate a fatal connection error MUST use a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame if it has sufficient state to do so.
previous_clause: A server crash or outage might result in clients continuing to send data to a server that is unable to properly continue the connection.
next_clause: To support this process, the server sends a stateless_reset_token value during the handshake in the transport parameters.

target_clause: The integrity check algorithm MAY change for other versions of the protocol.

previous_clause: ACK frames MAY appear in packets of any encryption level other than 0-RTT, but can only acknowledge packets which appeared in that packet number space.
next_clause: All other frame types MUST only appear at the 1-RTT levels.

target_clause: This pseudo-header field MUST be included in all responses; otherwise, the response is malformed ([malformed]).
previous_clause: For responses, a single ":status" pseudo-header field is defined that carries the HTTP status code; see Section 15 of [SEMANTICS].
next_clause: HTTP/3 does not define a way to carry the version or reason phrase that is included in an HTTP/1.1 status line.

target_clause: A server MUST discard an Initial packet that is carried in a UDP datagram with a payload that is less than the smallest allowed maximum packet size of 1200 bytes.
previous_clause: Datagrams containing Initial packets MAY exceed 1200 bytes if the client believes that the network path and peer both support the size that it chooses.
next_clause: A server MAY also immediately close the connection by sending a CONNECTION_CLOSE frame with an error code of PROTOCOL_VIOLATION; see [immediate-close-hs].

target_clause: Packets containing discarded CRYPTO frames MUST be acknowledged because the packet has been received and processed by the transport even though the CRYPTO frame was discarded.
previous_clause: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint is unable to buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY discard that CRYPTO frame and all CRYPTO frames received in the future, or it MAY close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.

target_clause: Receipt of a DUPLICATE_PUSH frame on any other stream MUST be treated as a connection error of type HTTP_FRAME_UNEXPECTED.
previous_clause: The DUPLICATE_PUSH frame is always sent on a request stream.
next_clause: A client MUST NOT send a DUPLICATE_PUSH frame.

target_clause: CONTINUATION frames MUST be associated with a stream.
previous_clause: The CONTINUATION frame changes the connection state as defined in [FieldBlock].
next_clause: If a CONTINUATION frame is received whose stream identifier field is 0x0, the recipient MUST respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.

target_clause: Sending keys MUST be updated before sending an acknowledgement for the packet that was received with updated keys.
previous_clause: If a packet is successfully processed using the next key and IV, then the peer has initiated a key update. The endpoint MUST update its send keys to the corresponding key phase in response, as described in [key-update-initiate].
next_clause: By acknowledging the packet that triggered the key update in a packet protected with the updated keys, the endpoint signals that the key update is complete.

target_clause: Each Push ID MUST only be used once in a push stream header.
next_clause: If a push stream header includes a Push ID that was used in another push stream header, the client MUST treat this as a connection error of type H3_ID_ERROR; see [errors].

target_clause: Applications to register codepoints in QUIC registries MAY include a codepoint as part of the registration.
previous_clause: For codepoints that are encoded in variable-length integers ([integer-encoding]), such as frame types, codepoints that encode to four or eight bytes (that is, values 2^14 and above) SHOULD be used unless the usage is especially sensitive to having a longer encoding.
next_clause: IANA MUST allocate the selected codepoint if the codepoint is unassigned and the requirements of the registration policy are met.

target_clause: An acknowledgment for a 1-RTT packet MUST be carried in a 1-RTT packet.
previous_clause: For instance, a client cannot send an ACK frame in a 0-RTT packet, because that can only acknowledge a 1-RTT packet.
next_clause: A server SHOULD treat a violation of remembered limits ([zerortt-parameters]) as a connection error of an appropriate type (for instance, a FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR for exceeding stream data limits).

target_clause: A server MUST treat receipt of a stateless_reset_token transport parameter as a connection error of type TRANSPORT_PARAMETER_ERROR.
previous_clause: A client MUST NOT include a stateless reset token.

target_clause: Once a connection exists to a server endpoint, this connection MAY be reused for requests with multiple different URI authority components.
previous_clause: For best performance, it is expected that clients will not close connections until it is determined that no further communication with a server is necessary (for example, when a user navigates away from a particular web page) or until the server closes the connection.
next_clause: To use an existing connection for a new origin, clients MUST validate the certificate presented by the server for the new origin server using the process described in Section 4.3.4 of [SEMANTICS].

target_clause: However, a GOAWAY MAY be sent first to provide additional detail to clients.
previous_clause: For unexpected closures caused by error conditions, a QUIC CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MUST be used.
next_clause: If a connection terminates without a GOAWAY frame, the last stream identifier is effectively the highest possible stream identifier (as determined by QUIC’s MAX_STREAM_ID).

target_clause: A PRIORITY frame MUST identify a client-initiated, bidirectional stream.
previous_clause: A PRIORITY frame MAY identify a Stream Dependency ID using a Stream ID of 0; as in [RFC7540], this makes the request dependent on the root of the dependency tree.
next_clause: A server MUST treat receipt of PRIORITY frame with a Stream ID of any other type as a connection error of type HTTP_MALFORMED_FRAME.

target_clause: Implementations MAY send stream types before knowing whether the peer supports them.

Recipients of unknown stream types MAY abort reading of the stream with an error code of H3_STREAM_CREATION_ERROR or a reserved error code ([http-error-codes]), but MUST NOT consider such streams to be a connection error of any kind.
next_clause: However, stream types that could modify the state or semantics of existing protocol components, including QPACK or other extensions, MUST NOT be sent until the peer is known to support them.

previous_clause: When adding a value to the Cache-Status header field, caches SHOULD preserve the existing field value, to allow debugging of the entire chain of caches handling the request.
next_clause: Depending on the deployment, this might be a product or service name (e.g., ExampleCache or "Example CDN"), a hostname ("cache-3.example.com"), an IP address, or a generated string.

target_clause: If an endpoint’s buffer is exceeded during the handshake, it can expand its buffer temporarily to complete the handshake. If an endpoint does not expand its buffer, it MUST close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.
previous_clause: Being unable to buffer CRYPTO frames during the handshake can lead to a connection failure.
next_clause: Once the handshake completes, if an endpoint is unable to buffer all data in a CRYPTO frame, it MAY discard that CRYPTO frame and all CRYPTO frames received in the future, or it MAY close the connection with a CRYPTO_BUFFER_EXCEEDED error code.

target_clause: An endpoint that migrates away from a local address SHOULD retire all connection IDs used on that address once it no longer plans to use that address.
